title: European Larch: Ancient European Larches You Can Visit
meta_description: Lithuania's tallest tree, at 49 metres, is a larch planted in 1849. Three European larches mapped, from a state forest to a Reykjavik cemetery.
intro: A larch drops its needles every winter, which is unusual for a conifer and part of why the ones that get noticed tend to stand out. Lithuania's State Protected Areas Service records one in the forest near Degsne at 49 metres, the tallest tree of any kind in the country, grown from a stand planted in 1849. Krakow's grows on a slope that was fenced off as woodland between 1902 and 1909 and kept shut to walkers for roughly half a century before the park finally let people in. Reykjavik's stands in Holavallagardur, the city's oldest cemetery, where conifers generally struggle against Iceland's wind and thin soil badly enough that the national forestry society singled this one out in 2011 for having managed it anyway.
